item.title: Study opens up new perspectives for targeted care of women with gestational diabetes
item.description: An international research team led by the Medical University of Vienna has shown that continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) in women with gestational diabetes can reduce the risk of a newborn with above-average birth weight.

item.title: Injectable scaffold vaccine shows strong protection against implant-related MRSA
item.description: Research reveals that silica scaffolds can train the immune system against S. aureus, offering a novel approach to prevent orthopedic device infections.

item.title: Single-dose dengue vaccine will benefit populations in hard-to-reach regions
item.description: A world-first single-dose vaccine against the dengue virus, manufactured and approved for use in Brazil, will especially benefit populations in hard-to-reach regions of the country such as the Amazon, say disease specialists.

item.title: Understanding how adult brains adapt to challenge and change
item.description: In a revelatory Genomic Press Interview published today in Brain Medicine, Dr. Paul Lucassen, full professor at the University of Amsterdam and leader of the Brain Plasticity group, shares his scientific journey that helped transform our understanding of how adult brains adapt to challenge and change.

item.title: UCL study reveals the challenges faced by London's night workers
item.description: A major new study by UCL researchers has revealed the challenges faced by London's 1.3m night workers, including pay inequality, health problems, transport difficulties, safety concerns and a lack of workplace dignity.

item.title: Doctors' critical thinking skills gets eroded with overreliance on generative AI
item.description: Overreliance on generative AI risks eroding new and future doctors' critical thinking skills, while potentially reinforcing existing data bias and inequity, warns an editorial published in the online journal BMJ Evidence Based Medicine.

item.title: Current state, challenges, and future directions of heart transplantation in USA and Western Europe
item.description: In nearly 60 years, heart transplantation has transformed from a daring vision to an established surgical procedure. Since the first adult heart transplant in the United States was performed at Stanford Hospital in 1968, the field has made significant strides.

item.title: Preloading Instacart online grocery carts with healthy ingredients could help improve the diets of families
item.description: University at Buffalo researchers have shown that preloading Instacart online grocery carts with healthy ingredients could be a useful tool for improving the diets of families with young kids at risk for obesity.

item.title: Common childhood virus linked to bladder cancer later in life
item.description: Tackling a common childhood virus could open the door to preventing bladder cancer, according to new research funded by Kidney Research UK and York Against Cancer.

item.title: University of Iowa research finds an effective therapy for rare kidney disease in children
item.description: A rare and life-threatening kidney disease in children finally has an effective therapy, thanks in large part to pioneering research and clinical leadership from University of Iowa Health Care Stead Family Children's Hospital.
